chunks: Al-Saffar from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Abu Hammam Isma'il ibn Hammam said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Regarding a man who marries a woman and marries his son to her daughter, then he divorces her, and another man marries her afterwards, and she bears a daughter from him. He disliked that one of his sons marry her, because she was his wife and he divorced her, so she became like a father to her, and before that he was a father to her.' This report is explicit regarding dislike, according to what we have previously established. And that which indicates the permissibility of this, also in addition to what we have established, is what he narrated:

key_terms.يُفَارِقُهَا: he divorces her / separates from her

ai.seo_question: Can a man's son marry the woman his father divorced after marrying the son to her daughter?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the complex kinship dynamics of *mut'ah* or temporary marriage arrangements in early Shia jurisprudence, where a father-in-law's divorce from his daughter's mother creates a quasi-parental bond. The text highlights the scholarly debate regarding whether this specific relational shift prohibits the son from marrying the woman, citing reports that suggest both dislike (*karahah*) and permissibility (*jawaz*). It serves as a key example of how marital alliances can create intricate legal impediments (*mahramiyah*) beyond direct lineage.
